moat_against: No pricing power: CMS/PAMA sets rates, cuts of up to 15% proposed from Jan 1, 2027
Routine testing commoditized; Labcorp is a near-equal rival for the same contracts
Low switching costs for physicians and patients on routine tests
Wage/labor inflation — Q2 2026 operating margin fell to 15.1% from 15.9%
Hospital customers can insource or re-bid outreach work at renewal
moat_for: National scale — one of two national labs, ~2,400 patient service centers, dense logistics network
Payer and health-plan access built over decades steers volume
Health-system embedding — Co-Lab partnerships and the Corewell joint venture raise switching costs
Advanced diagnostics breadth (Haystack MRD, AD-Detect, esoteric testing)
Automation / Invigorate program targeting ~3% annual productivity gains
moat_justification: National scale and cost advantage in a Labcorp duopoly, embedded health-system relationships and an advanced-test menu — but payers/CMS set the price, routine testing is commoditized, and Labcorp bids for every contract. Narrow moat, weak pricing power.
name: Quest Diagnostics Inc
one_liner: Durable duopoly cash generator, moat 6/10 — but priced past its super-bull case: weighted IRR 8.8%, IV@15% $113 vs $233 price; it clears 15% only at $113 or below.
